papers.title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: Developed an adapted weight-drop mouse traumatic brain injury model compatible with EEG/EMG recording that shows cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and diffuse axonal injury, and found that sodium oxybate treatment over the first 3 days after trauma increased slow-wave activity and reduced axonal injury, whereas chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons did not reduce slow-wave activity.

papers.title: State-dependent gating of sensory and cortical inputs by median raphe neurons
papers.summary: Characterized state-dependent responses of serotonergic, Vglut3 glutamatergic, and GABAergic median raphe neurons to sensory and cortical stimulation in vivo, showing larger responses during slow-wave sleep than wakefulness, with 5-HT neurons suppressed and Vglut3/GABAergic neurons activated by sensory stimuli, and optogenetic prefrontal input inhibiting 5-HT while exciting Vglut3 neurons during slow-wave sleep.

papers.title: Ideal sleep duration as a potential explanation of the bimodal chronotype: An exploratory study.
papers.summary: Reanalyzed questionnaire data from 1583 children/adolescents and 2115 adults to test whether bimodal chronotypes represent a distinct circadian typology category or a byproduct of ideal sleep duration, finding bimodal types overrepresented among short and long sleepers and underrepresented among medium sleepers, suggesting bimodality may reflect individual differences in ideal sleep duration.

papers.title: Pooled sequencing reveals patterns of underlying genomic divergence in Drosophila chronotypes
papers.summary: Used pooled DNA sequencing on 12 replicate Drosophila melanogaster populations experimentally evolved for early/morning versus late/evening emergence to identify genomic regions under selection, finding that early chronotype populations accumulated polymorphisms in photosensitivity, sleep, and circadian clock genes, while late chronotype populations accumulated polymorphisms in circadian clock, mRNA splicing, and ecdysis genes.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Proxies of Cortical Excitability in Epilepsy: Group Discrimination, Temporal Stability and Medication Sensitivity
papers.summary: Compared eight EEG-derived cortical excitability markers across 1404 recordings from 96 people with epilepsy and 85 healthy controls, finding that aperiodic offset and exponent were the only measures with robust group differences and were more reproducible across sessions in epilepsy, while higher antiseizure medication burden was associated with higher relative alpha power.

papers.title: [Research progress on genome-wide association study of circadian chronotype in adolescents].
papers.journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]
papers.summary: This review summarizes genome-wide association study (GWAS) findings on circadian chronotype, describing its genetic architecture and known variants in core clock genes, neurotransmitter signaling, and protein degradation pathways. It highlights the limited evidence in adolescents and discusses associations of evening chronotype and delayed circadian timing with insufficient sleep, depression, anxiety, and attention deficits.

papers.title: Wearable-based sleep and activity tracking detects Parkinson's disease and associated pathological hallmarks
papers.summary: Using passive wrist accelerometry-derived sleep and activity metrics, the authors trained a machine learning model (SAM-PD) that distinguished Parkinson's disease from controls with AUROC 0.93 and generalized to an independent European cohort (AUROC 0.95). The model performed comparably to the MDS prodromal PD risk score in detecting dopaminergic deficit and alpha-synuclein pathology, with REM sleep duration, walking cadence, and low-level acceleration as top predictors.

papers.title: The Effect of Nursing-Implemented Swaddling and Dim Light on Sleep Patterns and Weight Gain in Preterm Infants: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
authors: Aziza Ibrahim Abd El Kader Mohamed
papers.summary: This quasi-experimental study of 60 preterm infants found that nursing-implemented swaddling combined with dim light exposure was associated with significantly greater improvements in sleep-wake behavioral organization over five days and higher mean body weight at Day 5 and discharge versus routine NICU care.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node - in electrophysiology, contractility, metabolism, intracellular signalling and extracellular matrix
papers.summary: In mouse and human atrioventricular nodes, the authors showed a day-night rhythm in PR interval and identified a local circadian clock, with Bmal1 knockout reducing the PR-interval rhythm by ~43-52% and Kcnj5 knockout ruling out a major vagal role. Rhythmic transcripts, proteins (~15% of 4,186), ion channels, and reduced L-type Ca2+ current during sleep, supported by computer modeling, were found to underlie slowed nodal conduction at night.

papers.title: Associations of Serum Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid and Docosahexaenoic Acid Levels with Pediatric Sleep Disorders: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 95 children with sleep disorders, younger children had higher serum GABA and DHA levels, and children with insomnia had lower serum GABA than those with parasomnia, while DHA did not differ between these groups. The authors note that these correlational findings cannot establish causality and require further biomarker studies.

papers.title: Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention.
papers.summary: Developed a virtual reality replica (V-MSE) of a prior real multisensory environment intervention and characterized EEG spectral and nonlinear responses in 31 healthy participants pre- and post-exposure. The alpha/beta ratio increased significantly in both settings; in the V-MSE, frontal theta and theta/beta ratio also rose while relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity fell, supporting feasibility but not yet equivalence of V-MSEs.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity alterations in multiple system atrophy revealed by resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: Analyzed resting-state EEG and fMRI in 123 multiple system atrophy patients (discovery and validation cohorts) versus 69 controls, finding reduced delta power and widespread increases in theta and high gamma power plus decreased amplitude-based connectivity across alpha, beta, and gamma bands. Interpretable stacking models accurately classified MSA-C versus MSA-P subtypes and predicted UMSARS progression, identifying EEG as a promising disease-monitoring biomarker.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and behavioral analyses link perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) exposure to circadian and visual pathway disruption in larval zebrafish (Danio rerio).
papers.summary: Exposed larval zebrafish to 0.1-100 µg/L perfluorobutanoic acid for seven days and assessed development, behavior, and transcriptomics, finding non-monotonic hypoactivity at low concentrations and 3,177/1,919/2,277 differentially expressed transcripts at 0.1/1/10 µg/L. Low-dose exposure altered circadian rhythm and photoperiodism pathways, with cry2, cry3b, and cryba1a differentially expressed, linking PFBA to circadian and visual pathway disruption.

papers.title: Multiscale neural and endocrine control of CD8⁺ T cell fate in cancer: from systemic physiology to local immune circuits.
papers.summary: Reviews how autonomic and sensory neural circuits and the endocrine system regulate CD8+ T cell priming, trafficking, metabolism, and exhaustion across anatomical compartments, integrating sympathetic/parasympathetic/sensory axes, the HPA axis, metabolic hormones, and gonadal steroids. Proposes neuro-endocrine signaling as an actionable, mechanistically stratified layer of systemic immune regulation and a source of biomarkers and pharmacological targets for sensitizing tumors to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

papers.title: Daridorexant in treatment refractory cluster headache: A retrospective case series.
papers.summary: Retrospective before-after case series of 10 patients with treatment-refractory cluster headache and nocturnal attacks given add-on daridorexant, showing nocturnal attacks decreased from 13.1 to 6.4 per week, quality-of-life scores rose from 37% to 61%, and HIT-6 scores fell from 62.0 to 48.8, with adverse events in 3/10 patients. Suggests a potential adjunctive role for the dual orexin receptor antagonist, pending prospective controlled studies.

papers.title: Nocturnal hypoxaemic parameters from cardiorespiratory holter monitoring are associated with all-cause mortality in post-ischaemic stroke patients: The CHUTE study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 1113 patients hospitalised for first ischaemic stroke who underwent cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring, nocturnal hypoxaemia markers were associated with all-cause mortality: mean nocturnal SpO2 <90% (HR 1.46), ODI ≥15/h (HR 1.58), and T90 ≥10% (HR 1.34). Desaturation duration and slope were not significantly associated with mortality.

papers.title: Maniform Presentation of Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia Mimicking Late-Onset Mania: A Diagnostic Challenge.
papers.summary: A case report of a 70-year-old woman with no prior psychiatric history presenting with a first maniform episode mimicking late-onset bipolar disorder, whose neuropsychological testing showed executive dysfunction and MRI showed bilateral frontal and anterior temporal atrophy consistent with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia. The case illustrates the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing late-onset mania from neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Associations between biomarkers, muscle function, dynapenia status, fall risk, depressive symptoms, and sleep quality in patients with lower limb osteoarthritis: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 114 older adults with lower limb osteoarthritis awaiting joint replacement, 55.3% had poor sleep quality. Lower haemoglobin (OR 0.64), lower HbA1c (OR 0.57), and higher fall risk scores (OR 1.14) were independently associated with poor sleep quality in multivariable logistic regression.

papers.title: [Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea syndrome and myofunctional rehabilitation: A preliminary survey of French practitioners].
papers.summary: A preliminary national online survey of 135 French orthodontists, maxillofacial physiotherapists, and speech therapists assessed perceptions and practices of orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) in paediatric obstructive sleep apnoea. Orofacial hypotonia (91%) and lingual motor immaturity (88%) were the most frequently reported dysfunctions, and barriers to OMT included limited specialist access, training, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

papers.title: Using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health Framework to Document Real-World Functional Outcomes in Inpatient and Outpatient General Rehabilitation.
papers.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
keywords: International Classification of Functioning Disability and Health
papers.summary: A retrospective secondary analysis of implementation-pilot data from 674 inpatient and 601 outpatient general rehabilitation patients used ICF qualifiers to document functional outcomes. Significant reductions were observed in Body Functions codes (e.g., pain, sleep, joint mobility, muscle power) and in Activities and Participation codes, while Environmental Factors were stable facilitators.

papers.title: Orgasmic Meditation, Sleep, and Next-Day Somatic Distress: A 30-Day Observational Study.
papers.summary: In a 30-day observational study of 36 experienced Orgasmic Meditation practitioners (1,026 participant-nights), OM practice was not significantly associated with app-assessed sleep quality, duration, onset, or regularity. On mornings after OM, participants reported less body dissociation and less agitation, and a composite Factor 2 score was lower after OM (b = -0.77), though the estimate weakened when allowing between-participant variation.

papers.title: Association Between Sleep Quality and Personality Traits in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Stages 1-4: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 311 patients with CKD Stages 1-4, sleep disorder prevalence was 50.8%. Neuroticism and psychoticism were independently associated with higher PSQI scores, and personality traits explained an additional 5.6% of PSQI variance beyond sociodemographic and disease-related factors in a final model explaining 53.9%.

papers.title: Multimodal data integration for diagnosis and risk prediction of major depressive disorder in the UK Biobank.
papers.summary: Using multimodal data (proteomics, metabolomics, lifestyle, family history, biochemical measures, polygenic risk scores) from 30,040 UK Biobank participants, machine learning models achieved a mean time-dependent AUC of 0.679 for 15-year incident MDD prediction and 0.791 for prevalent diagnosis. Modifiable lifestyle factors, especially sleep patterns, and proteomic profiles outperformed polygenic risk scores; inflammatory mediators dominated diagnosis while neuroplasticity and metabolic markers predicted future risk.

papers.title: International Surgical Sleep Society Position Statement: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Adults.
papers.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This International Surgical Sleep Society position statement reviewed 43 studies on hypoglossal nerve stimulation for adult obstructive sleep apnea, reporting surgical response ranging from 67% to 83% and adherence of 5.6 to 7.7 hours per night. It concludes HNS is safe and effective as part of comprehensive OSA management, with mixed evidence on predictors of success.

papers.title: Climate change anxiety and insomnia in nursing students: implications for health promotion?
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 512 nursing students in Turkey, climate change anxiety was moderately positively correlated with insomnia severity (r = 0.372) and predicted 13.9% of insomnia severity variance. Insomnia severity was also associated with short or long sleep duration, smoking, chronic mental disorders, and screen exposure.

papers.title: Symptom Impact in Angelman Syndrome: Results from the Hope in Action Caregiver Survey.
papers.summary: A global online caregiver survey (Hope in Action, n=370) ranked symptom impact in Angelman syndrome, identifying expressive communication, seizures, mobility, sleep, and toileting as top treatment priorities. It reports the largest caregiver-reported assessment of unmet need and symptom burden to inform patient-focused drug development and trial outcome selection.

papers.title: [Guided orthodontic-surgical management of hyperdivergent skeletal class II malocclusion with obstructive sleep apnea: A case report].
papers.summary: A case report describes guided orthodontic-surgical treatment of hyperdivergent skeletal class II malocclusion with obstructive sleep apnea, using orthodontic decompensation followed by patient-specific guided surgery with counterclockwise rotation of the palatal plane and mandibular corpus and no intermediate splints. It shares the diagnostic and planning method for managing this complex case with reduced risk.

papers.title: Prevalence of suboptimal health status and its association with insomnia and smartphone addiction among medical students in Palestine: A multi-university cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: A multi-university cross-sectional survey of 461 medical students in Palestine found 47.5% with suboptimal health status, with insomnia (AOR 7.26) and smartphone addiction (AOR 2.48) independently associated with SHS in multivariable logistic regression. The authors call for longitudinal research and sleep- and digital-health-focused interventions.

papers.title: Management of Recurrent Depressive Disorder, Anxiety, and Insomnia in a Patient With Philadelphia Chromosome-Positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia Receiving Dasatinib Therapy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report describes a 55-year-old woman with Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukaemia on dasatinib who developed recurrent depression, severe anxiety, insomnia, and fatigue, and improved after individualised psychopharmacological adjustment accounting for drug-drug interactions and QT prolongation risk plus multidisciplinary psychiatric rehabilitation. It highlights psychiatrist-oncologist collaboration in managing psychiatric comorbidity during oncological treatment.

papers.title: Harnessing Circadian Resilience for Demand-Flexible Controlled Environment Agriculture
papers.summary: Using historical electricity market and wind-generation data, the authors tested demand-flexible photoperiod strategies (demand-side response events, cost-optimised and wind-optimised lighting) in controlled environment agriculture, finding preserved circadian rhythms and minimal effects on fresh or dry weight in basil, lettuce, mustard greens, and rocket. The results support demand-side energy flexibility in total controlled environment agriculture without substantial crop productivity losses.

papers.title: The Effects of Mind-Body Exercise on the Management of Fibromyalgia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 randomized controlled trials (1,177 fibromyalgia patients) found that mind-body exercise significantly improved pain, fatigue, sleep, anxiety, depression, and quality of life. Subgroup analyses showed Tai Chi/qigong and Pilates/yoga had comparable efficacy for pain and anxiety, while Tai Chi/qigong additionally improved depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Correction: Caffeine and modafinil ameliorate the neuroinflammation and anxious behavior in rats during sleep deprivation by inhibiting the microglia activation.
papers.summary: This is a published erratum correcting an earlier article on caffeine and modafinil ameliorating neuroinflammation and anxious behavior in sleep-deprived rats via inhibition of microglial activation. It contains no new findings beyond the correction notice.

papers.title: Association between the dietary index for gut microbiota and circadian syndrome: a cross-sectional study from NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.summary: In 18,491 US adults from NHANES 2007–2018, higher dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) scores were inversely associated with circadian syndrome (highest vs lowest quartile OR=0.693, 95% CI 0.603–0.797). Mediation analysis suggested that BMI and, to a lesser extent, systemic immune-inflammation index partly accounted for this association.

papers.title: Use of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions: an evidence map of systematic reviews.
papers.summary: This evidence map of 13 systematic reviews found high-certainty evidence only for abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation, and moderate-certainty evidence for acupressure/auricular acupressure improving sleep in cancer and chronic kidney disease and for massage reducing depressive symptoms in dementia. Most other conclusions for non-painful conditions were supported by low- or very-low-certainty evidence.

papers.title: Identification of associative factors for recurrent respiratory tract infection using machine learning models in preschoolers.
papers.summary: Using data from 15,075 Chinese preschoolers across two cross-sectional surveys (RRTI prevalence 14.55%), this study applied 10 machine learning models and found XGBoost performed best (AUC=0.733). SHAP analysis identified sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration as the top three factors associated with recurrent respiratory tract infection.

papers.title: Criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, and misclassification patterns of the International Fitness Scale in adolescents from a rural Mediterranean region of Spain: The EHDLA study.
papers.journal: Journal of exercise science and fitness
papers.summary: Evaluated the International Fitness Scale (IFIS) against objective ALPHA-Fit testing in 1017 rural Spanish adolescents, finding weak-to-modest criterion validity (overall rho=0.369; flexibility rho=0.635) and limited discriminative accuracy (AUC 0.66). Perception-accuracy discordance was common (36.1%), with underestimation linked to shorter sleep and concordant-low fitness linked to higher BMI and sedentary time.

papers.title: Comparing Fatigue Assessment Tools in Hemodialysis: Implications for Nephrology Practice From the Technology Assisted Stepped-Collaborative-Care Trial.
papers.summary: In 160 hemodialysis patients from a randomized controlled trial, SONG-HD-fatigue and PROMIS-fatigue showed psychometric properties comparable to FACIT-F, with strong correlations to related outcomes. However, only PROMIS-fatigue and FACIT-F detected significant treatment differences at 3 months, while SONG-HD-fatigue did not capture treatment response.

papers.title: Translating Geroscience Into Clinical Practice: Molecular Targets, Emerging Therapies, and Lifestyle Strategies for Healthy Longevity.
papers.summary: Critical narrative review synthesizing molecular geroscience, experimental therapeutics, biomarkers, and lifestyle factors for healthy longevity, framed within an expanded 12-hallmark aging network. It concludes that geroprotectors such as senolytics, NAD+ augmentation, mTOR inhibition, metformin, and spermidine lack definitive evidence for lifespan extension in healthy humans, whereas fitness, strength, diet quality, sleep, and cardiometabolic risk management have stronger human-outcome support.

papers.title: Quality of Life as a Pathway Linking Sleep Quality and Depressive Symptoms in Medical University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: Used cross-sectional structural equation modeling in 150 medical university students to test whether quality of life mediates the sleep quality–depressive symptoms association, finding an indirect-only mediation pattern through QOL (indirect beta=0.229) with no significant direct path. Longer screen time was also associated with poorer sleep quality (beta=0.338).

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: Protocol for a single-center, single-blind randomized controlled trial randomizing 90 chronic insomnia disorder patients stable on zolpidem 1:1 to acupuncture or sham acupuncture alongside zolpidem tapering over 8 weeks with 4-week follow-up. The primary outcome is the zolpidem discontinuation rate at week 8, with secondary outcomes including taper reduction rates, Insomnia Severity Index, anxiety/depression scales, and sleep diary measures.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
